data.current_description:
Use this endpoint to get information about the card or network token that enables you to decideon the routing of the transaction and the eligibility of the card for the type of transaction.

If you include [your supported brands](https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/#/CheckoutService/latest/post/cardDetails__reqParam_supportedBrands) in the request, the response also tells you if you support each [brand that was identified on the card](https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/#/CheckoutService/latest/post/cardDetails__resParam_details).
 
If you have an API-only integration and collect card data, use this endpoint to find out if the shopper's card is co-branded. For co-branded cards, you must let the shopper choose the brand to pay with  if you support both brands.
data.summary_suggestion: Retrieve card brand and co-brand details
data.description_suggestion: Retrieves card or network token information including brand identification and co-brand detection. Accepts card data and optional list of supported brands. Returns identified card brands, co-brand status, and whether each brand is supported by your integration. Use this endpoint to determine transaction routing eligibility and enforce brand selection for co-branded cards. Supports API-only integrations with card data collection.
data.reasoning: Original summary is passive ('Get') and incomplete - doesn't mention co-brand detection which is a key use case. Description is verbose and unclear about inputs/outputs. Improved version uses action-oriented language, clearly specifies what inputs are expected (card data, supported brands list), what outputs are returned (brand identification, co-brand status, support status), and the primary use case (routing and co-brand handling). Better for AI agent decision-making.

data.current_description:
Takes in the donation token generated by the `/payments` request and uses it to make the donation for the donation account specified in the request.

For more information, see [Donations](https://docs.adyen.com/online-payments/donations).
data.summary_suggestion: Process a donation using a donation token
data.description_suggestion: Processes a donation transaction using a donation token previously generated by a `/payments` request. Requires the donation token and target donation account identifier in the request. Completes the donation for the specified account and returns the transaction result. This endpoint is the second step in the donation flow - first create a payment with donation intent to obtain the token, then use this endpoint to finalize the donation.

data.current_description:
This operation takes the origin domains and returns a JSON object containing the corresponding origin keys for the domains. 
> If you're still using origin key for your Web Drop-in or Components integration, we recommend [switching to client key](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/client-side-authentication/migrate-from-origin-key-to-client-key). This allows you to use a single key for all origins, add or remove origins without generating a new key, and detect the card type from the number entered in your payment form.
data.summary_suggestion: Generate origin keys for domain authentication
data.description_suggestion: Generates origin keys for specified domain origins to enable client-side authentication in Web Drop-in or Components integrations. Accepts a list of origin domains and returns corresponding origin keys for each domain. Each key is bound to its specific origin for security validation. Note: This operation is legacy - Adyen recommends migrating to client keys which support multiple origins with a single key and provide enhanced functionality.
